key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on composition and mixing order: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide helps passivate the surface.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor chemistry and addition sequence could help preserve MXene additives during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track surface chemical changes.
Apply density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS analysis and DFT calculations indicate rapid degradation with iodine/polyiodides, slower oxidation with PbI2, and hydrogen-bond-mediated passivation with MAI.
watch_item: The abstract reports model-ink chemistry, not quantified solar-cell performance gains; precursor addition order requires careful control.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
